title: career.json
description: A durable, evidence-backed record of one career. The pack is the product; resumes are disposable projections of it.

employment.description: Employers, titles, and dates. These are the most background-checkable facts on a resume and previously lived nowhere in the pack, so generation supplied them from source text with no evidence ID. Every date, title, and employer in an artefact must trace to a record here.

private_profile.description: Contact and identity details for the subject. Created during setup, never published in a public artefact, and included in full only in a document sent to a named recipient. A pack without this cannot produce a sendable resume.

location.description: City and country as it should appear on an artefact.

address.description: Never appears in any artefact, public or private.

photo_reference.description: Never appears in any artefact, public or private.

skill_vocabulary.description: Canonical skill names mapped to their aliases. Free-text skills fragment as a pack grows ('threat modelling' and 'threat modeling' becoming different things), which quietly breaks recall.

education.description: Qualifications. Absent from the schema until 2026-09-06, so a degree could not be recorded at all and JSON Resume's education section could never be filled.

path.description: Workspace-relative file path, the URL for a url source, or for a person source the review record holding what was said.

character_count.description: Characters of extracted text, not the file size on disk. Record the file size in byte_size.

retrieved.description: Date a url source was checked, or a person source was spoken to. Required for both, because neither has a hash: it is the only thing that makes them auditable.

independent.description: True when the source is not authored or controlled by the subject. A resume and a LinkedIn profile are both self-authored and neither is independent.

saved_copy.description: For a url source: workspace-relative path of a saved copy of the page, so excerpts can be verified offline. The URL stays in path.

evidenceAtom.description: evidence_status and external_safe are required so that an atom cannot fail open past the publication guard.

metrics.description: A metric is a claim, and a claim whose denominator nobody recorded cannot be defended. A plain string is still valid, so existing packs need no migration; the object form exists so the basis has somewhere to live rather than being reconstructed in an interview.

value.description: The metric as it would appear in a document.

basis.description: How it was measured: the baseline, the denominator, the period, and who produced it. null means not recorded, which is honest; omitting the field says nothing.

measured.description: False where the figure is an estimate or a recollection rather than something a system produced.

evidence_status.description: self_asserted: appears only in material the subject wrote, however many times. corroborated: a named third party or public artefact supports it, but no auditable record is captured. externally_verified: supported by an independent source recorded in source_records with independent: true. unresolved: an open question. declined: the subject chose not to pursue it. Repetition across the subject's own resume and LinkedIn is not corroboration.

corroborators.description: Who or what would confirm this claim in a reference check or interview. Empty means nobody has been identified, which is a commercial risk, not a schema error.

reference.description: Role or artefact, not a personal name unless the subject supplied one for this purpose.

outcome_type.description: activity: how much work happened (engagements run, tasks defined). output: what was produced (patterns, artefacts, courses). business_outcome: what changed for the organisation (risk reduced, revenue, time-to-market, incidents avoided). Hiring managers discount activity metrics; prefer business_outcome when selecting evidence.

role_fit_notes.description: Where this evidence counts against the subject as well as for them. Media reach and speaking volume read as strength for a field or advocacy role and as a negative signal for a hands-on engineering role.

notes.description: Operator note about how this atom must be handled. Not candidate-facing text, and never carried into the selection view; a constraint the generator must obey belongs in `constraints`.

open_questions.description: Unanswered questions blocking this atom. Required in practice for unresolved atoms, which is what makes unresolved actionable rather than a shrug.

employment_id.description: The employment record this happened during. Gives the atom a date without duplicating one.

occurred.description: When this happened. A pack that cannot answer this cannot do recency, ordering, or gap detection, which is most of what a career memory is for.

inferred.description: True when the dates were taken from the employment window rather than recorded directly. An inferred nine-year window is barely an answer; narrow it when the detail is still fresh.

capture.description: How this atom entered the pack. Annual write-ups are the main capture event, so knowing which review period produced an atom is what makes the next import able to skip it.

note_id.description: The capture note this was promoted from.

tags.description: Narrative threads that cut across employers, such as scaling-teams or incident-response. Skills describe the work; tags describe the story it belongs to.

constraints.description: Reviewed handling constraints a generated claim must respect: 'prototype only, did not reach production', 'team contribution, do not imply sole ownership'. These reach the selection view. Operator `notes` do not, which is why the two are separate fields.

employer.description: The name as it should appear on an artefact.

employer_of_record.description: The entity that actually paid the subject, where it differs from the name on the artefact. A background check compares against this, not the client.

end.description: 'present' for a current role. Null means unknown, which is a gap to resolve, not a current role.

parent_employment_id.description: For a promotion within one employer, so a progression can be collapsed without losing the detail.

scope.description: Facts about the size of the role, which a background check can test like dates and a recruiter reads first: team size, direct reports, budget owned, organisation size, geography. Rendered on the role line by make-resume. Cold screens asked for these on every draft; atoms had nowhere to put them.

remit.description: What the function formally owns: gates, standards, patterns, control paths. The thing a head-of screen asks for first.

educationRecord.description: A qualification. Recorded separately from evidence atoms for the same reason employment is: a degree is not a STAR achievement, it is a fact a background check verifies, and it needs provenance rather than a narrative.

institution.description: The name as it should appear on an artefact.

qualification.description: MSc, BSc, diploma, certification. The award, not the subject.

end.description: Year awarded. 'present' for study in progress.

grade.description: Distinction, honours class, GPA. Only where the subject supplied it.
